edits.content:
## Parse Quantifiers and Scope
- Rewrite each option mentally with its quantifiers explicit. Distinguish “for every” from “there exists,” “both” from “at least one,” and almost-sure claims from positive-probability claims.
- Track modifiers such as “eventually,” “once,” and “for every index.” Do not replace an eventual or conditional conclusion with a stronger unconditional one.
- In a classification, distinguish “the limit lies in this set almost surely” from “each member of the set is attained with positive probability.”

## Compare the Entire Conclusion
- When asked for the strongest statement, compare claims by implication and verify that every added clause follows from the hypotheses. A stronger-sounding adjective is not evidence that the claim is true.
- Check scope carefully: local versus global regularity, continuity on an open versus closed interval, finite-time blow-up versus failure of global boundedness, and uniform versus parameter-dependent constants are distinct conclusions.
- Do not infer preservation of a property in a limit merely from convergence; verify that the stated convergence controls that property.

## Quick Consistency Checks for Exact Claims
- For identities, compare total weights or degrees on both sides before attempting a derivation. Substitute the smallest admissible parameter values as a quick way to expose false universal claims.
- Expand notation carefully, especially zero-length blocks, and preserve the exact order of indices or factors. Similar-looking permutations need not be equivalent.
- For formulas involving counts, check whether the definition counts a distinguished endpoint or origin; avoid silently changing a count to include or exclude it.

## Quantitative Bounds and Edge Cases
- Compare the exact stated rate, coefficient, and dependence of constants; a generic big-O-looking alternative may be weaker than a sharper explicit estimate.
- Test important regimes such as the initial time, a transition scale, and large time, and verify that the proposed bound is meaningful uniformly over the full stated domain.
